marketing_evidence: B2B OEM acoustic/electronic components; little evidence
rationale: Ampacs International is a Vietnam-based OEM maker of speaker and acoustic components and appears to be Taiwanese-owned. It is a B2B contract manufacturer with no consumer brand and no published financials, so its F1 fit is weak.

marketing_evidence: Large Brazilian helmet/moto-parts brand (30,000+ SKUs, reps in every state); motorcycling events and rally collections, no major sponsorship confirmed
rationale: Pro Tork is a Brazilian helmet and motorcycle-parts maker that calls itself Latin America's largest moto-parts factory, with 38+ years in business. It has motorsport credibility and a strong Brazil presence (Sao Paulo GP), but its revenue is undisclosed and it is mostly domestic.

marketing_evidence: little evidence for AUXPOW brand; parent AUX known for air-conditioner marketing
rationale: AUXPOW (auxsmart.com) is a power/electrical-equipment business of China's AUX Group. Brand-level revenue is not disclosed and it is scored only on itself; its B2B energy and grid products have limited consumer overlap with F1.

marketing_evidence: Heavy domestic brand advertising; launched EV motorbikes (2023) and G3 EV SUVs (2025); sister Djarum unit owns Como 1907
rationale: Polytron is Djarum's Indonesian electronics brand: 10,000+ staff, TVs and appliances, smartphones, laptops, and since 2023-25 EV motorcycles and SUVs. The EV push gives it some technology-showcase angle, but it sells almost only in Indonesia and does not disclose revenue.

marketing_evidence: B2B suit/tailored-clothing OEM for international labels; little evidence
rationale: Silver Crest Clothing is a Bengaluru-based contract maker of tailored suits and jackets for overseas fashion labels. With no consumer brand and no published financials, it has little F1 sponsorship logic.
itc Group (Guangzhou) makes professional public-address, conference and intelligent audio systems for B2B projects worldwide. It has a niche venue-audio angle at best and discloses no revenue.

marketing_evidence: Cross Jeans fashion brand marketing in Europe; little sponsorship evidence
rationale: Sik Makas is a Turkish denim manufacturer that owns the Cross Jeans brand, sold in European retail. It is a mid-market apparel company with no published revenue and only partial overlap with F1's affluent audience.

marketing_evidence: B2B OEM helmet maker (ERT, Conehead, Biodome technologies); little evidence
rationale: Strategic Sports is a Hong Kong-headquartered OEM maker of cycling, snow and powersports helmets with its own impact-protection technologies. It supplies global brands rather than consumers and discloses no financials.

revenue: unknown (c. BRL 1.3B reported around the 2019 judicial-recovery filing; retail chain later sold to Oscar Calcados)
profitability: Strained: in judicial recovery since 2019 (BRL 638.5M debts), still listed 'em recuperacao judicial' in 2025
rationale: Grupo Paqueta is a Brazilian footwear maker that has been in judicial recovery since 2019 and sold its retail stores to Oscar Calcados in 2023. Its strained finances rule out a major sponsorship budget.

revenue: unknown (private; c. 4M travellers/year, 6,000+ staff, 37 companies in 21 countries)
marketing_evidence: Major consumer travel brand in Russia, CIS, Europe and Turkey markets; no major sports sponsorship confirmed
rationale: Coral Travel Group (formerly OTI Holding) is a large private Turkish tour operator and hotel group serving about 4 million travellers a year across 21 countries, with brands including Coral Travel, Odeon, Ferien Touristik and Seven Seas. Consolidated turnover is not published, though its scale suggests a large business; travel and hospitality give it reasonable activation potential.
